basis: Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, microcephaly and cerebral atrophy; abnormal visual evoked potentials do not establish ocular damage.
Inherited keratinization disorder affecting skin and nails.
Bone sclerosis and marrow failure define disease; visual impairment and hearing loss reported in 80-99%; neurologic, dental and skin findings omitted by cap.
Congenital intestinal secretory dysfunction; choanal atresia affects 10/22 (~45%) and corneal erosion 9/22 (~41%).
Definition specifies the anemic form of erythroblastosis fetalis, an immune-mediated destruction of fetal red cells.
INS-related monogenic diabetes; diabetic organ complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Inherited multisystem autoimmunity; no specific damaged organ is established as common across the included subtypes.
Pure hair-and-nail ectodermal dysplasia; alopecia and nail abnormalities occur in all seven annotated patients.
Inherited focal epilepsy arising during sleep; no established extra-neurologic organ damage.
Unbalanced placental vascular connections produce intertwin blood transfer and circulatory imbalance; permanent cardiac, renal or brain injury is not universal.
Congenital suprabulbar paresis causes swallowing and speech dysfunction; reflux and glue ear are separate conditions, without established intrinsic GI injury.
Epithelial carcinoma occupying lymph nodes; no mapped organ of origin is specified. Nodal location alone does not establish blood-cell malignancy or lymphoma.
Inherited retinal degeneration encompassing cone-rod, macular and retinitis pigmentosa phenotypes.
Combined immunodeficiency and hyper-IgE syndrome; provided evidence does not establish additional organ damage meeting the frequency threshold.
Broad carcinoma group chiefly arising in oral cavity/salivary glands or pharyngeal/laryngeal/sinonasal airways; rarer anatomical subtypes are not generalized.
Congenital gonadotropin deficiency; persistent olfactory dysfunction from developmental olfactory defects affects roughly half of patients, including Kallmann forms.
SETBP1 neurodevelopmental disorder; visual impairment in 14/29 (~48%) and hypermetropia in 9/29 (~31%) support ocular involvement.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, present in all 16 annotated patients.
Dysraphic lipomatous malformation involving the conus spinal cord; no additional organ involvement meeting the threshold is established.
Ovarian epithelial tumor of a reproductive organ; no endocrine function or other mapped organ involvement is specified.
Autoimmune platelet destruction; purpura is a bleeding sign. Arterial thrombosis is a separately diagnosed complication, not intrinsic cardiovascular involvement.
Persistent exophthalmos is an orbital eye-adnexal disorder; no underlying endocrine or immune cause is specified.
NPHS2-related podocyte disease causes nephrotic syndrome and commonly renal failure; secondary lipid abnormalities do not establish another damaged organ.
Focal autoimmune stiff-person spectrum disorder; rigidity and spasms reflect impaired neural inhibition rather than primary skeletal muscle damage.
Epilepsy, intellectual disability and dental enamel defects define the syndrome; hypohidrosis indicates sweat-gland dysfunction in 30-79%.
